p.src: Now Inspector He, having received the prefect's orders, came down from the hall and at once went to the confidential office to confer with the others. The constables said, “The lakes and marshes around Shijie Village lie hard by Liangshan Marsh, and all about them stretch boundless reed beds and waterways. Without a large force of government troops, boats, cavalry, and men, who would dare go there to seize the bandits?” After hearing them, He Tao said, “That is true enough.” He returned to the hall and reported to the prefect, “It appears that the lakes by Shijie Village adjoin Liangshan Marsh itself, and the whole region is filled with deep channels, branching waterways, reed beds, and grassy swamps. Even in ordinary times men are robbed there, to say nothing of now, when that band of outlaws has joined them. Unless a large body of troops is raised, how could anyone dare go there and make arrests?” The prefect said, “If that is so, I shall appoint another capable patrol inspector for the suppression of banditry, assign him five hundred officers and men, and send him with you to make the arrests.” Inspector He received the order and returned to the confidential office. Summoning all the constables, he selected more than five hundred men and sent each to prepare provisions and weapons. The next day, the patrol inspector received an official warrant from Jizhou Prefecture. Together with Inspector He, he mustered five hundred soldiers and all the constables, and they set out as one for Shijie Village.

p.src: Meanwhile, after Chao Gai and Gongsun Sheng had set fire to the manor, they took more than ten retainers and headed for Shijie Village. Halfway there they encountered the three Ruan brothers, each bearing a weapon, who had come to meet and escort them home. All seven men gathered at Ruan Xiaowu's farmstead. By then Ruan Xiao'er had already moved the old and young of the family into the marsh. The seven discussed going to seek refuge at Liangshan Marsh. Wu Yong said, “At present, Zhu Gui, the ‘Dry-Land Crocodile,’ keeps an inn at the Lijia Crossing, where he receives brave men from every quarter. Anyone wishing to join the band must first go to him. Let us ready some boats, load all our belongings aboard, and take gifts for him so that he may introduce us.”

p.src: While they were discussing their flight to Liangshan Marsh, several fishermen suddenly came to report, “Government troops are racing toward the village!” Chao Gai sprang to his feet and cried, “Since those wretches have pursued us here, let us not flee!” Ruan Xiao'er said, “Never fear! I shall deal with them myself. I will send most of those wretches to drown and spear the rest to death.” Gongsun Sheng said, “Do not panic! Just watch what this humble Daoist can do!” Chao Gai said, “Brother Liu Tang, you and the Learned Master should load the valuables and the families into the boats and pole straight to the left side of Lijia Crossing to wait for us. We shall see how matters develop and follow shortly.” Ruan Xiao'er selected two sculling boats and loaded his mother, the rest of his family, and the household valuables aboard. Wu Yong and Liu Tang each took charge of one boat. They ordered seven or eight attendants to row them to Lijia Crossing and wait there. He then instructed Ruan Xiaowu and Ruan Xiaoqi to pole their small boats and…meet the enemy in this manner. The two each took a boat and departed.

p.src: Meanwhile, He Tao and the patrol inspector led the government troops toward Shijie Village. As they drew near, they saw boats at the river landing and seized every one of them. They ordered the soldiers who could handle themselves on the water to board the boats and advance. The troops and horses moved along the banks while the boats kept pace with them, advancing by water and land together. When they reached Ruan Xiao'er's house, they raised a concerted battle cry and rushed in together, only to find the dwelling already deserted, with nothing inside but a few heavy, cumbersome household articles. He Tao said, “Go and seize some fishermen from the neighboring households.” When questioned, they said, “His two brothers—Ruan Xiaowu and Ruan Xiaoqi—both live out in the marsh, and there is no reaching them without a boat.” He Tao conferred with the inspector, saying, “The marsh has many branching channels and a bewildering maze of routes; what is more, no one knows the depths of its swamps, slopes, and pools. If we scatter in pursuit, I fear we shall fall into the bandits' trap. Let us leave men to guard all the horses here in the village, while the rest of us board the boats together.” Thereupon the patrol inspector, Inspector He, and all the constables boarded the boats together.

p.src: They had seized well over a hundred boats. Some were poled and others rowed, and together they all headed toward Ruan Xiaowu's fishing hamlet. Before they had crossed five or six li of open water, they heard someone singing a mocking song among the reeds. The men halted their boats to listen, and the song went: All my life I fish in the smartweed shallows; I sow no green grain, nor do I plant hemp. I shall slay every cruel magistrate and corrupt official, and with a loyal heart repay His Majesty Zhao.

p.src: Inspector He and all his men were startled when they heard it. Far off they saw a lone man sculling a small boat toward them as he sang. Someone who recognized him pointed and said, “That is Ruan Xiaowu.” He Tao waved his hand, and the men strained forward together, each brandishing his weapon as they went to meet him. Ruan Xiaowu laughed loudly and cursed them: “You thieving officials who torment the common people—how dare you be so brazen! What have you come to provoke your lord for? Are you not plucking a tiger's whiskers?” Behind He Tao were men skilled with bow and arrow. They nocked their arrows, drew their bows to the full, and loosed together. When Ruan Xiaowu saw the arrows coming, he seized his oar, somersaulted, and dived beneath the water. The men rushed up, but caught nothing.

p.src: They had not passed two more branching channels when a whistle sounded from the reed-flower marsh. The men spread out their boats and saw two men approaching in a single craft. At the bow stood a man wearing a green bamboo-leaf hat and a green straw rain cape. Twirling a slim-shafted spear in his hand, he too sang: Your lord was born and raised in Shijie Village; by nature, he was born to kill. First I shall cut off the heads of He Tao and the inspector, then bear them to the capital and present them to the sovereign of Zhao.

p.src: Inspector He and all his men were startled once again. Looking together, they saw the man in front twirling his spear and singing, while the man behind worked the oar. Someone who knew him said, “That is Ruan Xiaoqi.” He Tao shouted, “All of you, press forward together and seize this bandit first! Do not let him escape!” Ruan Xiaoqi heard him and laughed, “You scoundrel!” With a mere flick of his spear, he signaled the boat to turn, and it darted away into a narrow channel. The men raised a shout and gave chase. Ruan Xiaoqi and the man rowing with him worked the oar as if in flight, whistling as they sped onward through the maze of narrow channels.

p.src: The officers and soldiers chased this way and that until they saw that the waterway had narrowed. He Tao said, “Hold! Moor the boats for now, all along the bank.” When they went ashore to look, they saw nothing but boundless reeds, with not the slightest trace of a path on dry land. He Tao grew suspicious and could reach no decision, so he questioned the local villagers. They replied, “Though we live here, even we do not know all the many ways through this place.” He Tao then ordered two small boats rowed out, each carrying several constables, to scout the way ahead. More than four hours passed after they left, but no report came back. He Tao said, “Those wretches are good for nothing!” He sent another five constables in two more boats to scout the route. These constables rowed off in the two boats, but after more than another two hours there was still no report at all. He Tao said, “These men are all seasoned constables, sharp and capable. How can they be so witless as not to send even one boat back with a report? And to think that every one of the officers and soldiers brought here is just as hopelessly confused!”

I shall have to make the journey myself.” He chose a swift little boat and several veteran constables, each armed with a weapon. With five or six birchwood oars rising and falling, He Tao sat in the bow as they swept into the reed-filled waterway.

p.src: By then the sun had already sunk in the west. They rowed some five or six li across the water and saw a man approaching along the bank, carrying a hoe. He Tao called, “You there! Who are you? What place is this?” The man replied, “I am a farmer from this village. This place is called Dead End Ditch. The way goes no farther.” He Tao asked, “Did you see two boats come this way?” The man said, “Have you not come to arrest Ruan Xiaowu?” He Tao asked, “How do you know we have come to arrest Ruan Xiaowu?” The man replied, “They are fighting in the black woods just ahead.” He Tao asked, “How much farther is it from here?” The man replied, “It is just ahead—you can see it from here.” Hearing this, He Tao ordered the boat brought alongside so that they could go to the others’ aid. He sent two constables ashore carrying forked polearms. The man suddenly raised his hoe, and with one blow apiece sent both constables tumbling head over heels into the water. He Tao was startled. He sprang up and was about to leap ashore when the boat suddenly drifted away. A man shot up from beneath the water, seized He Tao by both legs, and with a single tug sent him plunging backward into the water. The others in the boat were about to flee, but the man with the hoe pursued them aboard and struck them down one after another, smashing out their brains. The man beneath the water dragged He Tao backward onto the bank, took off his sash, and bound him with it. The man who had been underwater proved to be Ruan Xiaoqi. The man on the bank carrying the hoe was Ruan Xiao’er.

p.src: The two brothers glared at He Tao and cursed him: “We three brothers have ever delighted in killing men and setting fires. What are the likes of you worth? How dare you deliberately lead the officers and soldiers here to arrest us!” He Tao pleaded, “Good sirs! I was sent under orders from above and had no choice in the matter. How would I ever dare come to arrest such heroes? Have pity: at home I have an eighty-year-old mother with no one else to support her. I beg you to spare my life!” The Ruan brothers said, “Tie him up like a rice dumpling for now and toss him into the cabin.” They flung all the corpses into the water. Each gave a shrill whistle, and four or five fishermen emerged from the reeds and boarded the boats. Ruan Xiao’er and Ruan Xiaoqi each steered one of the boats away.

p.src: Sand flew and stones raced; the waters coiled and the heavens shook. Pitch-black clouds massed across the sky; murky darkness drove on the sudden rain. Lotus leaves overturned, their green canopies jostling across the heart of the waves; Reed plumes thrashed, white banners whirling in confusion over the lake; The wind could snap the trees atop Mount Kunlun and awaken the venerable Dragon King of the Eastern Sea.

p.src: That uncanny wind swept in from behind. It blew so fiercely that everyone covered their faces in terror and cried out in distress, while all the mooring ropes snapped. Just when they were utterly at a loss, shrill whistles sounded behind them. Peering into the wind, they saw a broad glow of fire shoot out beside the reed plumes. The men cried, “This time we are finished!” The forty or fifty boats, large and small, were being driven by the gale into collisions with one another and could no longer be controlled. By then the fiery glow had already reached them. It came from a cluster of little boats lashed together in pairs and piled high with reeds, brushwood, and grass, all blazing and crackling as they rushed straight at them before the following wind. The forty or fifty government boats were massed together in a solid block, and the channel was so narrow that there was nowhere to evade the attack. There were more than ten of the largest vessels, and the fireboats were driven right into their midst and set them ablaze. Men hidden beneath the water were helping guide the fireboats forward. The blaze forced the officers and soldiers aboard the great ships to leap ashore and flee for their lives, only to find themselves surrounded by reeds and wild waterways, with no path on dry ground. Then the reeds on the banks also began to crackle and blaze. The bandit-catching officers and soldiers had no escape in either direction. With the wind howling and the fire raging, they could only force their way onward and stand crowded together in the mud.

p.src: Amid the blaze appeared a swift little boat. One man stood at the stern working the oar, while a scholar sat in the bow holding a gleaming sword and shouted, “Do not let a single one escape!” The soldiers huddled together in panic amid the mud. Before the words had died away, two men appeared on the eastern bank among the reeds, leading four or five fishermen, all advancing with gleaming swords and spears in their hands. On the western bank among the reeds came another two men, likewise leading four or five fishermen, all carrying gleaming flying-fish hooks. On the eastern and western banks, the four heroes and their men attacked together, thrusting down the line. In no time at all, they had stabbed the many officers and soldiers to death in the mud.

p.src: The two on the eastern bank were Chao Gai and Ruan Xiaowu; the two on the western bank were Ruan Xiaoer and Ruan Xiaoqi; and the gentleman aboard the boat was Gongsun Sheng, who had summoned the wind. The five heroes, leading more than a dozen fishermen from the village, speared every one of the government troops to death in the reed marsh. Only Inspector He remained, trussed up like a rice dumpling and thrown into a boat's hold. Ruan Xiaoer hauled him ashore, pointed at him, and cursed: “You wretch! You are a vile worm who cheats and torments the people of Jizhou! I meant to hack you into ten thousand pieces, but instead you shall go back and tell the thieving asses who govern Jizhou Prefecture that we three Ruan heroes of Shijie Village, and ‘Heavenly King Chao Gai’ of Dongxi Village, are not men to be trifled with! I will not enter your city to borrow grain, and he had better not come to our village seeking death! If he so much as casts an insolent eye our way, never mind a petty prefect like you—even if Grand Tutor Cai sends men to arrest us, or Cai Jing comes in person, I will stab twenty or thirty holes clean through him. We are letting you go. Do not come again! Pass that on to your damned official, and tell him not to court death! There is no main road here, so I shall have my brother escort you to where the road begins.” Ruan Xiaoqi then put He Tao aboard a small swift boat and took him straight to the main road, where he shouted: “Go straight on from here and you will find your way. We killed all the others; if we simply let you go unharmed, would not that thieving ass of a prefect laugh at us? So let us have your two ears as proof!” Ruan Xiaoqi drew the sharp knife at his side and cut off both Inspector He's ears, leaving him streaming with fresh blood. He sheathed the knife, untied the bonds, and released him onto the bank. A poem says: The government troops all found the ditch where severed heads lie; yet letting He Tao go unmarked would never do. They left him his ears to hear their words, then swiftly took the donkey's ears in place of its head.

Ruan Xiaoqi drew the sharp knife at his side and cut off both Inspector He's ears, leaving him streaming with fresh blood.
He sheathed the knife, untied the bonds, and released him onto the bank.
A poem says: The government troops all found the ditch where severed heads lie; yet letting He Tao go unmarked would never do.
They left him his ears to hear their words, then swiftly took the donkey's ears in place of its head.

p.src: Having escaped with his life, He Tao found his own way back to Jizhou.

u.src: Having escaped with his life, He Tao found his own way back to Jizhou.

p.src: Now Chao Gai, Gongsun Sheng, the three Ruan brothers, and the dozen or more fishermen all boarded five or seven small boats, left the waters of Shijie Village, and made straight for the Li Family Crossing. On arriving, they found the boats carrying Wu Yong and Liu Tang and joined company with them. Wu Yong asked how they had resisted the government troops, and Chao Gai related the whole affair in detail. Wu Yong and the others were overjoyed. After putting all the boats in order, they went together to seek refuge at the tavern of Zhu Gui, the “Dry-Land Crocodile.” When Zhu Gui saw so many men coming to ask admission to the band, he hurried out to welcome them. Wu Yong gave Zhu Gui a truthful account of their origins and adventures, which delighted him greatly. After introductions had been made one by one, he invited them into the hall and seated them, then hurriedly ordered the servers to prepare the customary wine and entertain them. He immediately brought out a leather-backed bow, nocked a whistling arrow, and shot it toward the reeds across the inlet. No sooner had the whistling arrow landed than a young bandit was seen rowing out in a boat. Zhu Gui hastily wrote a dispatch, listing in detail the names and number of the heroes seeking admission, and gave it to the young bandit to carry to the stronghold and report their arrival; meanwhile, he had a sheep slaughtered to feast the heroes.

p.src: After the night had passed, Zhu Gui rose early the next morning, summoned a large boat, and invited all the heroes aboard. Taking along the boats in which Chao Gai and his companions had come, he set off with them toward the mountain stronghold. After traveling for some time, they came to an inlet, where they heard drums beating and gongs sounding on the bank. Chao Gai looked and saw seven or eight young bandits rowing out in four patrol boats. On seeing Zhu Gui, they all saluted, then turned and went back ahead as before.

p.src: The party then reached Golden Sands Beach and went ashore, leaving their families, the boats, and the fishermen there to wait. Presently several dozen young bandits came down the mountain and escorted them up to the pass. Wang Lun led a group of chieftains out beyond the pass to welcome them. Chao Gai and the others hurriedly bowed. Returning the courtesy, Wang Lun said: “I am Wang Lun. I have long heard the illustrious name of ‘Heavenly King Chao’; it has rung in my ears like thunder. What joy that you should honor our humble stronghold with your presence today.” Chao Gai said: “I am an unlettered man, ignorant of the classics and histories, and exceedingly rough in my ways. Today necessity compels me to hide my shortcomings here. I would gladly serve as a common soldier under your command and count myself most fortunate if you did not reject me.” Wang Lun replied: “Say no more of that. Please come up to our humble stronghold, and we shall discuss matters further.” The whole company followed the two leaders up the mountain. When they reached the Hall of Righteous Assembly in the main stronghold, Wang Lun repeatedly deferred to Chao Gai and his party, asking them to take the places of honor above the steps. Chao Gai and his six companions formed a line on the right. Wang Lun and the chieftains formed a line on the left. After each had completed the courtesies, host and guests took their seats facing one another. Wang Lun summoned the junior leaders below the steps, and after they had saluted, drums and music began to play throughout the stronghold. First he ordered the junior leaders to go down the mountain and entertain the attendants who had come with the guests; separate lodgings below the pass were provided for their rest. A poem says: Those who join a band plainly form one company; if kept for their mettle, they should be treated as kin. Why then receive them merely as passing guests? Perhaps the host fears he cannot remain master.

p.src: Within the stronghold they slaughtered two oxen, ten sheep, and five pigs, and laid on a great feast amid loud drums and music. As the chieftains drank, Chao Gai told Wang Lun and the others everything that weighed upon his heart, from beginning to end. When Wang Lun had heard it all, he sat aghast for a long while. Torn by indecision, he could not speak, but brooded in silence and merely went through the motions of answering and attending the feast. When the feast ended that evening, the chieftains escorted Chao Gai and the others to the guest lodge below the pass, where servants were ready to attend them.

p.src: Chao Gai was delighted and said to Wu Yong and the other five: “After committing so monstrous a crime, where could we have found shelter? Had Chief Wang not shown us such undeserved favor, we would all be homeless by now. We must never forget to repay this kindness!” Wu Yong merely gave a cold laugh. Chao Gai asked: “Why do you only laugh so coldly, Master? If something is amiss, you may tell us.” Wu Yong replied: “You are too straightforward, elder brother. Do you truly think Wang Lun means to take us in? Do not look only at his intentions; observe his expression, his every movement, and his manner.” Chao Gai asked: “What did you see in his expression?” Wu Yong said: “Did you not notice that at first, when he spoke with you at the feast this morning, he seemed quite friendly; but afterward, when you told how you had killed so many government troops, including the bandit-suppression inspector, released He Tao, and how valiant the ‘Three Ruan Heroes’ were, his expression changed somewhat. Though he answered agreeably enough, his bearing and manner showed that his heart was very far from his words. Had he truly meant to take us in, he would have settled our positions this very morning. Du Qian and Song Wan are both rough fellows. What would they understand of receiving guests? Only Lin Chong, once an instructor of the Imperial Guards in the capital, is a man from a great city who understands the ways of the world; yet circumstances have forced him to occupy merely the fourth seat. This morning, when Lin Chong saw how Wang Lun responded to you, indignation arose in him. He kept glancing at Wang Lun and brooded inwardly. As I judge him, he does have some thought of looking after us, but his hands are tied. I need only drop a few words to make the men of this stronghold turn upon one another.” Chao Gai said: “We depend entirely upon your ingenious strategy to find us a place here.” That night the seven men retired to rest.

p.src: At daybreak the next morning, someone came to report, “Instructor Lin has come to visit.” Wu Yong said to Chao Gai, “He has come to sound us out. He has fallen into our plan.” The seven men hurriedly rose to welcome him and invited Lin Chong into the guest lodge. Wu Yong stepped forward and thanked him, saying, “We are deeply indebted for your kindness last night and ashamed to have troubled you.” Lin Chong said, “It was I who failed in courtesy. Though I wished to serve you properly, I was unfortunately not in a position to do so. I beg your forgiveness.” Scholar Wu said, “Though we are men of little worth, we are not senseless trees and grass. How could we fail to see the chief’s special regard and solicitude for us? Our gratitude is profound.” Chao Gai repeatedly urged Lin Chong to take the seat of honor, but Lin Chong would not hear of it. He pressed Chao Gai into the upper seat and settled himself in the lower one. Wu Yong and the other five seated themselves in a row. Chao Gai said, “I have long heard of the instructor’s great name and never expected that I would meet you today.” Lin Chong said, “When I formerly lived in the Eastern Capital, I always observed the proper courtesies in my dealings with friends and never failed in them. Although I have now had the honor of seeing you, I cannot fulfill my lifelong wish. That is why I have come especially to speak with you.” Chao Gai thanked him, saying, “I am deeply grateful for your generous regard.”

p.src: Wu Yong then asked, “I had long heard that when you were in the Eastern Capital, you were a hero of the first order. How did you come to fall out with Gao Qiu and suffer his persecution? Later I heard that at Cangzhou the army fodder depot was burned down, likewise through his scheming. And afterward, who recommended that you come up to the mountain?” Lin Chong said, “As for that villain Gao Qiu’s persecution of me, the mere mention of it makes my hair stand on end, for still I cannot avenge this wrong! That I found refuge here is entirely because Lord Chai recommended me.” Wu Yong said, “This Lord Chai—can he be Chai Jin, known throughout the rivers and lakes as the ‘Little Whirlwind’?” Lin Chong said, “The very man.” Chao Gai said, “I have often heard that Lord Chai upholds righteousness, gives freely of his wealth, and welcomes heroes from every quarter. They say he is a direct descendant of an emperor of the Great Zhou. If only I could meet him once!”

p.src: Wu Yong then said to Lin Chong, “Lord Chai is a man whose fame fills the four seas and whose renown spreads throughout the realm. If your martial skill were not peerless, Instructor, why would he have recommended you to this mountain? I do not say this merely to flatter you: by rights Wang Lun ought to yield the foremost chieftain’s seat to you. That is the common judgment of all under heaven, and it would also honor Lord Chai’s letter.” Lin Chong said, “I am obliged by your generous words, sir. Yet I committed a grave crime and fled to Lord Chai. It was not that he would not keep me; I feared that I might implicate him and cause him trouble, so I volunteered to come up the mountain. I never imagined that today I would find myself with nowhere either to go or to stay! It is not my low rank that troubles me. Wang Lun is simply fickle in purpose and unreliable in speech, making it hard to remain together.” Wu Yong said, “Chief Wang seems all affability in his dealings with others. How can his heart be so narrow?” Lin Chong said, “Today Heaven has blessed this stronghold by bringing so many heroes here to lend mutual aid. It is like flowers added to brocade, or rain falling upon parched seedlings. But that man harbors only jealousy of the worthy and resentment of the capable, fearing that the heroes’ power will overshadow his own. Last night, when he heard you speak of how your company had killed the government troops, he took exception to it and showed signs that he did not intend to keep you. That is why he had you brought down below the pass to lodge.” Wu Yong said, “Since Chief Wang feels that way, we need not wait for him to dismiss us. We shall leave of our own accord and seek refuge elsewhere.” Lin Chong said, “Gentlemen, do not think yourselves strangers. I, Lin Chong, know what must be done. I feared only that you might decide to withdraw, and so I came early to tell you. Today we shall see how he treats you. If the scoundrel speaks reasonably and behaves differently from yesterday, the matter shall end there; but if he utters so much as half a word amiss this morning, leave everything to Lin Chong.” Chao Gai said, “Chief, we are all deeply grateful for such extraordinary kindness.” Wu Yong said, “For our brothers’ sake, we are causing you to fall out with your old comrades. If we can be accepted, let us be accepted; if not, we shall take our leave at once.” Lin Chong said, “You are mistaken, sir! The ancients said, ‘The discerning cherish the discerning; heroes cherish heroes.’ What use can that vile wretch, that filthy beast, ever be? Gentlemen, set your minds at ease for now.” Lin Chong rose and took leave of them, saying, “We shall meet again shortly.” They all saw him out, and Lin Chong went back up the mountain alone. Indeed:

p.src: Chao Gai asked Wu Yong, “Sir, how shall this meeting turn out?” Scholar Wu laughed and said, “Rest easy, elder brother. This meeting may well make you master of the stronghold. Today Instructor Lin is certainly minded to kill Wang Lun in a clash. Should his resolve falter, with my three-inch, never-rotting tongue I shall leave him no choice but to do it. Each of you, elder brother, conceal a weapon about your person. When you see me raise my hand and stroke my beard as the signal, join forces at once.” Chao Gai and the others secretly rejoiced.

Having dressed themselves neatly, they set out for the feast. Then Song Wan himself rode up on horseback to invite them once more, while the minions brought seven mountain sedan chairs. The seven men entered the chairs and went straight to the water fort on the southern mountain. p.src: Before long, three or four men returned, one of them carrying a large tray on which lay five great ingots of silver. Wang Lun rose and offered Chao Gai a cup, saying, “We are deeply honored that you heroes have come here to join our brotherhood. I only regret that our humble mountain stronghold is but a shallow pool—how could it harbor so many true dragons? We have prepared this trifling gift and earnestly hope you will deign to accept it. Pray seek rest at some greater stronghold; I shall personally send men to offer my submission there.” Chao Gai replied, “I have long heard that your great mountain welcomes worthy and able men, and so we came straight here expressly to seek refuge and join your band. If you cannot accommodate us, we shall take our leave of our own accord. As for the silver you have so generously bestowed, we would never dare accept it. I do not mean to boast of wealth, but we still have some traveling money at our disposal. Please take back this generous gift at once. We bid you farewell here and now.” Wang Lun said, “Why do you refuse it? It is not that our humble mountain refuses to receive you heroes. It is only that provisions are scarce and lodgings few; I fear we might fail you in days to come and cause you embarrassment. That is why I dare not ask you to stay.”

Chao Gai replied, “I have long heard that your great mountain welcomes worthy and able men, and so we came straight here expressly to seek refuge and join your band. If you cannot accommodate us, we shall take our leave of our own accord.

I do not mean to boast of wealth, but we still have some traveling money at our disposal.
Please take back this generous gift at once. We bid you farewell here and now.”
Wang Lun said, “Why do you refuse it?

It is not that our humble mountain refuses to receive you heroes. It is only that provisions are scarce and lodgings few; I fear we might fail you in days to come and cause you embarrassment. That is why I dare not ask you to stay.”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Lin Chong’s brows shot upward and his eyes opened wide. Seated in his armchair, he roared, “When I first came up the mountain, you likewise claimed that provisions were scarce and lodgings few. Now that Brother Chao and these heroes have come to the stronghold, you trot out the very same words again. What possible reason is there for this?” Wu Yong said, “Chief, calm your anger. The fault is naturally ours for coming here and thus harming the harmony within your stronghold. Today Chief Wang is courteously sending us down the mountain and even giving us traveling money; he has not driven us away harshly. Please calm yourself, Chief. We shall simply depart.” Lin Chong said, “This man hides a knife behind his smile—his words are fair, but his deeds are foul! I will not let him escape me today!” Wang Lun shouted, “Look at this brute! You are not even drunk, yet you use such words to insult me. Have you utterly forgotten the order between superior and subordinate?” Lin Chong cried furiously, “You are nothing but an impoverished scholar who failed the examinations, with no learning in your breast. How are you fit to be master of this stronghold?” Wu Yong said, “Brother Chao, because we came up the mountain seeking refuge, we have instead caused the chief to lose face. Let them ready the boats at once, and we shall take our leave.”

p.src: Chao Gai and the other six men rose and made to leave the pavilion. Wang Lun urged them to stay, saying, “Please at least finish the banquet before you go.” With a single kick Lin Chong sent the table flying aside. He sprang to his feet, drew a gleaming blade from beneath his robe, and brandished it in a blazing fury. Wu Yong stroked his beard with one hand. Chao Gai and Liu Tang came back up into the pavilion and made a show of barring Wang Lun’s way, crying, “Do not fight among yourselves!” Wu Yong seized Lin Chong by one arm and said, “Chief, you must not act rashly!” Gongsun Sheng pretended to remonstrate, saying, “Do not ruin the cause of honor on our account.” Ruan Xiao’er moved to keep Du Qian occupied, Ruan Xiaowu did the same to Song Wan, and Ruan Xiaoqi held Zhu Gui in check. The lesser bandits were so terrified that they could only stare, dumbfounded.

Gongsun Sheng pretended to remonstrate, saying, “Do not ruin the cause of honor on our account.”
Ruan Xiao’er moved to keep Du Qian occupied, Ruan Xiaowu did the same to Song Wan, and Ruan Xiaoqi held Zhu Gui in check. The lesser bandits were so terrified that they could only stare, dumbfounded.

p.src: Lin Chong seized Wang Lun and cursed him: “You are a wretched rustic scholar who owes even your arrival here to Du Qian. Lord Chai gave you such generous support, supplied your traveling expenses, and befriended you; yet when he recommended me to you, you still raised objection after objection. And now, when these heroes have come expressly to join us, you mean to send them down the mountain as well. Do you think Liangshan Marsh belongs to you alone? You jealous thief, envious of every worthy and able man—what use is there in letting you live? You possess neither magnanimity nor great ability and are unfit to be master of this stronghold!” Du Qian, Song Wan, and Zhu Gui had meant to step forward and intervene, but those men held them so tightly that they dared not move. Wang Lun tried to find a way to escape, but Chao Gai and Liu Tang blocked him. Seeing that the situation had turned against him, Wang Lun cried, “Where are all my trusted men?” There were indeed several trusted followers at his side who had meant to rescue him, but when they saw Lin Chong’s savage fury, not one dared step forward. Lin Chong held Wang Lun fast, cursed him once more, then drove his blade straight into his heart and felled him in the pavilion with a single thrust. Poor Wang Lun had been master of the stronghold for many years, only to die that day at Lin Chong’s hand, precisely fulfilling the ancient saying: “Great breadth of heart brings great fortune; deep scheming brings deep disaster.” A poem bears witness: Shameful the ambition to hold Liangshan alone; jealous of worth and scornful of talent, he knew little tolerance. He deemed the chieftain’s seat his private possession and treated the gathered heroes as bandits and foes. Amid the banquet’s merriment, murderous intent arose; where cups and platters clattered, a human head fell. His narrow heart was truly hateful; refusing to retain the worthy, he failed to retain his life.

p.src: When Chao Gai saw that Wang Lun had been killed, he and his companions all drew their blades. Lin Chong had already cut off Wang Lun’s head and held it aloft. Du Qian, Song Wan, and Zhu Gui were so terrified that they all knelt and said, “We are willing to follow you, elder brother, holding your whip and stirrup in service!” Chao Gai and the others hurriedly helped the three men to their feet. Wu Yong dragged the foremost armchair through the pool of blood, pressed Lin Chong into it, and proclaimed, “If anyone refuses to submit, let Wang Lun be his example! Today we shall establish Instructor Lin as master of the stronghold.” Lin Chong cried out, “Sir, you are mistaken! Today I slew this inhuman villain in our internal strife only because I placed loyalty to all these heroes above everything else. I truly had no intention of plotting to gain this seat. If Brother Wu now yields this first seat to me, Lin Chong, would that not invite the ridicule of every hero under heaven? If you mean to force me, I would sooner die! I have a few words to propose, though I do not know whether you gentlemen will agree to them.” The others replied, “Who would dare disobey what you say, Chief? We would gladly hear your proposal.”
